result:
My verdict for DG1 round 3 (T-DG1-REV-SEC-R3) is **PASS**: nothing has regressed since round 2, and I'm raising one new Low finding that doesn't block the gate.

**Identity check:** HEAD is `4f312cc`. Recomputing the candidate ID gives `sha256:18e15071…056f5b` (394 files) for the working tree, for HEAD, and for the commit the manifest records (`40dbd24`). The commits between those two only touch assignments, the manifest and `stages.json`. The record uses `40dbd24` as its commit, as round 2 did.

**What changed:** I compared the round-2 and round-3 manifests file by file. Exactly one file changed, `apps/web/e2e/journeys.spec.ts`. So the business-unit hierarchy guard and migration 0009, destination authorization, rate-limit keying, gate tooling and CI config are byte-identical to what I verified in round 2.

**The F-DG1-232 fix:** it only touches the end-to-end test.
- It now waits for the shell to finish loading after the reload before pressing Tab.
- It keeps every existing assertion and adds a stricter one: pressing Enter on the skip link must move focus to `main#main`, which can take focus (`Shell.tsx:99`).
- The added lines contain no secrets, URLs or risky code, and lint is clean.

**Checks:** all run in a throwaway clone that I deleted afterwards.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| typecheck, build, lint, OpenAPI lint, no-CDN, format | all exit 0 |
| Unit tests, Node 22 and Node 24 | 326/326 on each |
| Integration tests, twice, each on a fresh throwaway PostgreSQL 16 | 209/209 both times, including `bu-hierarchy-guard.test.ts` with migration 0009 applied |
| Gate and agent tool tests | 105/105 |
| Deploy-script tests | 59/59 |
| Offline install-sandbox suite | 13/14; the only failure is AC-1 (effect), the live-registry case documented as D-057 (recorded as a residual, not BLOCKED) |
| SBOM check | OK |
| Historical DG0 validation | PASS |
| The three `ci.yml` copies | byte-identical and unchanged since round 2; actually running CI is the documented residual D-058 |

My first install-sandbox run scored 8/14 because the default package store sits in the read-only home directory. I reran it against a scratch copy of the store, as round 2 did.

**New finding:**
- **F-DG1-147 (Low, not a mandatory violation, REQ-DLV-033):** no typecheck covers the end-to-end tests (`apps/web/e2e/**` and `playwright.config.ts`). `apps/web/tsconfig.json` only includes `src`, `test`, `vite.config.ts` and `vitest.config.ts`, and Playwright runs specs without checking types. A type error in a spec would therefore pass every static gate check and the CI typecheck job.
  - This gap predates this round. When I type-checked the current spec separately it had no errors.
  - Suggested fix: add an `apps/web/e2e/tsconfig.json` and include it in `pnpm -r typecheck`.
  - I numbered it F-DG1-147 in the code-security range; the orchestrator may renumber it.

There are no unresolved Critical, High or mandatory findings, and my round-2 findings (F-DG1-140 to F-DG1-146) stay closed.

The review record, findings file and narrative are in `docs/delivery/reviews/DG1/round-3/`; both JSON files validate against their schemas. Evidence logs are in `docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG1/code-security/round-3/`.

Files are in `docs/delivery/reviews/DG1/round-3/`:
- code-security-reviewer.json
- code-security-reviewer.findings.json
- code-security-reviewer.md
